game_concept: A survival strategy set in Eldritch Ruins – Moss Library, a ruined library: the tomb cartographer must handle cursed statues while practicing lists. Core idea – Index Archery: Hit targets by choosing the right list index, including negative ones.
theme: Eldritch Ruins – Moss Library: a ruined library
core_gameplay_loop: Construct a solution, execute it, inspect actual state and outputs, then revise until all mission goals pass.
secondary_mechanics: Hint tokens that reveal one line of code
player_objective: Declare char: declare resource as char, apply resource + 72, and print each result with %c. Dataset 7 starts with [0, 1, 2, 3]. Match every stream. Use a full main function and a return statement.
controls: Edit the C program. Run tests all streams; Step shows declarations, assignments and output. readInput() is a LogiCade game-port helper declared in logicade.h. This safe practice runtime supports a documented C subset.
win_condition: The executed solution satisfies every output and world-state check.
lose_condition: The available unsuccessful execution checks are exhausted.
assets_style: Shared Kenney CC0 tile and audio assets with deterministic Canvas layouts; assets are not duplicated per game.
duplicate_check_notes: Unique combination of primary mechanic 'Index Archery' (Week 7 slot 2), mission type 'Survival Siege', and setting 'Moss Library'. No other file shares this combination; games sharing the mechanic differ in mission/win condition and setting, and games sharing the setting use a different mechanic.
topic: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations

region.name: Eldritch Ruins
region.mood: eerie choir pads and stone-scrape stings

source_player_objective: Protect the relic vault from cursed statues in Moss Library: keep the arrows meter above zero by applying the concept correctly until the 54-second timer ends.
source_lose_condition: arrows drops to 0, or lives reach 0, before the 54-second timer ends.
hint: Declare before use. char resource = readInput(); creates the named game-port value; printf uses %c.
